faqs.a: Enter any two sides you know. A right triangle is fully determined by two sides, because the third side follows from the Pythagorean theorem and the angles from trigonometry.
faqs.q: What do I need to know to solve a right triangle?

faqs.a: Use the tangent: angle = arctan(opposite / adjacent). Opposite the side of length a with adjacent side b, angle A = arctan(a / b).
faqs.q: How do I find an angle from two sides?

faqs.a: The acute angles always add to 90 degrees, so the second angle is 90 minus the first. The right angle itself is always 90 degrees.
faqs.q: Why do the two acute angles add to 90 degrees?

faqs.a: Half the product of the legs: area = (a × b) / 2. The legs are perpendicular, so they serve as base and height.
Check the order: when you give a leg and the hypotenuse, the hypotenuse must be the longest side. Increase it or fix the leg value.
faqs.q: Why does the calculator show a note instead of answers?

right-triangle-calculator.formula:
c = √(a² + b²)
Angle A = arctan(a / b)
Angle B = 90° - A
Area = (a × b) / 2
Perimeter = a + b + c
howTo: Choose what you know: two legs, or a leg plus the hypotenuse.

keyFacts: Two sides fully determine a right triangle.
The hypotenuse comes from the Pythagorean theorem: c = √(a² + b²).
Angles come from inverse trig: A = arctan(a / b).
The two acute angles always sum to 90 degrees.
Area is half the product of the legs.

right-triangle-calculator.workedExample:
A right triangle has legs a = 3 and b = 4.

c = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5.
Angle A = arctan(3 / 4) ≈ 36.87°.
Angle B = 90° - 36.87° ≈ 53.13°.
Area = (3 × 4) / 2 = 6.
Perimeter = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12.

The classic 3-4-5 triangle, fully solved.
